title: The Mother's Eulogy in Cave Three

title_i18n.en: The Mother's Eulogy in Cave Three

subtitle: A Mother Carves an Empire into Stone
era: Year 19 of Vasishthiputra Pulumavi, c. late 1st-early 2nd century CE
moral: A woman's voice can preserve a king's fame.

sources.citation: R.G. Bhandarkar, Nasik Inscriptions, Epigraphia Indica Vol. 8 (1906)
sources.note: Primary publication of the Cave 3 prashasti and grant records.

sources.citation: Corpus Inscriptionum Indicarum Vol. IV: Satavahana inscriptions
sources.note: Official inscription corpus for the Nashik records.

sources.citation: D.C. Sircar, Select Inscriptions Vol. I (1965); Upinder Singh (2008)
sources.note: Translations and modern cautions on the eulogy's claims.

panels.shot: low-angle wide of a dim rock-cut hall with towering pillars, Gautami Balashri in the foreground touching a chisel-marked wall

dialogue.text: In the 19th year of Pulumavi, a mother named Gautami Balashri carved into stone a eulogy so fierce that it still argues with history.

panels.shot: slow push-in from cave entrance, framing Balashri against shadowed pillars and monks' cells

dialogue.text: This cave in the hills above Nasik was once a humming vihara. But its most enduring echo is not a monk’s sermon, it is a mother’s voice in stone.

panels.shot: medium close-up on Balashri’s face, half-lit by a bronze oil lamp

dialogue.text: She is Gautami Balashri, mother of Gautamiputra Satakarni, grandmother of King Vasishthiputra Pulumavi. Not a legend, but a name we can still read.

panels.shot: over-the-shoulder from behind Balashri, looking toward the wall with faint incised letters taking shape

dialogue.text: Her inscription in Cave Three begins as many grants do, with date and king. But soon the words swell into something else: a prashasti, a rolling wave of praise.

panels.shot: wide shot of the cave interior, monks and artisans faintly visible as silhouettes, Balashri central

dialogue.text: The record calls this the 19th year of her grandson Pulumavi. Yet the heart of the text looks back, to her son’s battles, her son’s titles, her son’s gifts.

panels.shot: close-up of Balashri’s hands resting on her lap, fingers lightly touching a folded palm-leaf manuscript

dialogue.text: She has not come unprepared. The phrases, polished and formal, are likely drafted before the rock is touched. This is not mere memory; it is public performance.

panels.shot: medium profile shot of Balashri, lips slightly parted as if dictating, artisan in foreground carving

dialogue.speaker: gautami_balashri
dialogue.text: Write of him as my son… but also as protector of this land.

panels.shot: tight shot on the inscription area showing early lines; camera angled so a few legible letters suggest Brahmi without being fully readable

dialogue.text: The lines call Gautamiputra ‘eka-bamhana’—the solitary or unique Brahmana. Later scholars will argue over the phrase, but the pride in it is unmistakable.

panels.shot: medium shot with imaginative backdrop: Balashri in present foreground, while faint, ghostly outline of a battle scene occupies the background

dialogue.text: She has the victories carved large: her son, it proclaims, broke the pride of Sakas, Yavanas, Pahlavas, humbled foreign lords and restored the Satavahana name.

panels.shot: low-angle dramatic shot of Balashri as if addressing unseen courtiers, with map-like mountains faint in the background

dialogue.text: The inscription names wide territories under his sway. But historians read with care: a prashasti stretches space as it stretches adjectives.

panels.shot: medium shot of Balashri and a Buddhist monk seated opposite each other near a pillar

dialogue.text: Yet this is not only a war-song. In the same stone she records grants to these monks, the feeding of the sangha, the building of cells and walks for the rainy season.

panels.shot: close-up on Balashri’s face, a slight softening in her eyes, background blurring

dialogue.text: Between lines of conquest, the prashasti names virtues: generosity, discipline, truthfulness. It praises her son as much for restraint as for the reach of his arm.

panels.shot: medium shot where Balashri gestures to the artisan to include lines about herself

dialogue.text: Then, quietly, she has her own qualities set down: devoted wife, firm in vows, giver of gifts. A woman refusing to vanish behind her men.

panels.shot: wide shot showing Balashri, artisans, and a few onlookers including a Satavahana official

dialogue.text: Her role is powerful, public, but not a formal queen on the throne. The inscription’s power lies instead in patronage, in who may speak for the dynasty in stone.

panels.shot: overhead shot of the cave floor, with Balashri rising slowly, lamp casting a long shadow

dialogue.speaker: gautami_balashri
dialogue.text: Let those yet unborn know his name… and mine with his.

panels.shot: slow push-in on the finished inscription surface, Balashri’s silhouette small at the edge

dialogue.text: When she steps away, the work is done. Her son is gone, her grandson reigns, but their story, filtered through her words, has been fixed into the hill itself.

panels.shot: time-lapse style wide shot: the cave mouth seen across centuries, with subtle hints of changing visitors

dialogue.text: Centuries pass. Empires rise and crumble. Yet readers in distant ages will bend over this wall, still hearing Gautami Balashri speak across two thousand years.

panels.shot: extreme close-up on a few clear Brahmi letters of her name, then pulling back to reveal the broader inscription

dialogue.text: To us, her eulogy is both window and warning: a crafted royal boast, not a literal map, yet one of the clearest, earliest women’s voices in Indian political history.

panels.shot: final contemplative shot of modern sky above the Nashik hills, faint overlay of Balashri’s calm face

dialogue.text: In her hands, a mother’s grief and pride became statecraft. She reminds us that sometimes the sharpest chisel on a king’s fame is not his sword, but a woman’s inscription.
